questions.answer: International House and other places

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Three meals per day are served at my dorm

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I can only speak about the International House. Some things that surprised me were the (low) quality of the food, and the safety (the elevators broke time and time again, and several intruders found their way into the dorm). 
I think it is important to consider that no matter how open a person is to other cultures, it can be a challenge to live in a small dorm room with a stranger from a completely different culture for a whole semester.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great options and systems, but availability was badly communicated

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's like looking through an online catalog and signing up for the ones you like

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the professors or administrative workers in charge of the courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into the courses I wanted to get into

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your chance, even if you don't believe that you will get accepted into the course. More often than not, the seats don't fill up and "unqualified" candidates get accepted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Insane amount of assignments, which all count towards the final grade

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were incredibly easy, and others were incredibly hard (compared to CS courses at KU).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nearly impossible to get into one, when you're leaving after 1 semester

questions.answer: A whole plethora of clubs were available - just not for exchange students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All types of events for international students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking and try to get out of Berkeley as much as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture was easy, adjusting to living with someone from a different culture (Singapore in my case) was way harder

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't try - it's impossible as they don't want to make friends with international students, so try to socialize with the other international students instead

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping all the time and that taxes are not included in the prices

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How fast you can get your food at restaurants

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make a schedule to keep track of your time
Attend events for international students
Bring twice the amount of money that you expect

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If I could go back in time, I think I would have chosen to go on exchange somewhere closer to home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made some new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living in a small room with a stranger for 4 months

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
